title: I Took the In-Law Seating Chart Through Rehearsal, Dinner, and the Car

parts.text: I found Grandma Rosa behind a speaker on a chart I had not approved. I am twenty-seven, binder in hand, hydrangeas, carpet cleaner smell. Elaine had rearranged cards at the late rehearsal. Jess the coordinator looked mint-gum tired. Malik was parking uncles. The hydrangeas were innocent. Elaine said photos mattered more than canes. Elaine said, "Don't touch my flowers" I said, "Rosa isn't a flower" I held Rosa's card like a ticket. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i. The door closer hissed the way office doors always hiss.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She is reaching for the card, and the original 2:14 file is still in my binder.

parts.text: Jess reprinted 2:14 while Elaine tore a duplicate into the vase. Ink bled. Malik saw it and went quiet-hot. Rehearsal continued with Rosa on the aisle. Elaine sat in the back texting the family chat about humiliation. I muted. The chafing fuel smell mixed with flowers, a cursed candle. Brooke took photos from row two and lived. Elaine demanded a redo of the whole walk. Jess said no, because time is a vendor. Malik said, "Mom doesn't get a secret chart" Elaine said, "I'm the mother" My shoes pinched. parts.text: I put a staffer on the cards and ate cake with Rosa. Elaine cried in a bathroom, then danced one song, then left early. Malik's kind mother ran day-of like a general with snacks. Nobody hid a cane. Weeks later a pressed hydrangea arrived with no apology. I filed it behind 2:14. Marriage is fine. Binders are a love language. The dental office still teases me about charts. I accept the bit. Photos look like a wedding, not a magazine that hates grandmothers. That was the assignment. Rosa said, "I heard everything" I said, "You were supposed to" Rosa squeezed my hand with the strength of people who have waited in worse lines.
